question: On 22 September 2026, Commissioner Šefčovič announced a ‘substantial agreement’ in discussions on the EU-Philippines free trade agreement. The information provided mentions an agreement to liberalise ‘over 94 % of tariff lines, covering more than 97 % of goods’, but no mention is made of a crucial sector: canning. In view of the above: 1.
When will the Commission publish the terms of the agreement?
What has the Commission agreed on seafood products – and canned tuna in particular – and what information has the Commission given the sector during negotiations?

What safeguards has the Commission included to prevent a negative impact on the EU canning sector, in view of the cumulative effects of this agreement, the agreement with Indonesia, and the agreements being negotiated with other countries in Southeast Asia?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.11.2026) On 22 September 2026, the EU and the Philippines reached substantial agreement on a free trade agreement following a video call between the Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security and the Philippine Secretary of Trade and Industry, who instructed their negotiating teams to finalise the agreement as soon as possible.

This work is currently ongoing and, once concluded, the formal conclusion of the negotiations will be announced. Pending the formal conclusion of the negotiations, the Commission cannot comment on the negotiated outcome for a given sector such as seafood products. After formal conclusion, the Commission will publish the outcome of the text negotiations on the website of DG Trade and Economic Security.

The Commission recalls that it has already published all its initial text proposals for the various chapters of the future free trade agreement between the EU and the Philippines on its website in 2024. The Commission is fully aware of the importance of the EU tuna processing industry, notably in coastal regions. Tuna remains sensitive in the negotiations, and the Commission is handling it accordingly.

The Commission takes into account the interests of the EU fleet and processing industry, the current and potential impact of imports, and the cumulative effect of preferential access granted under other agreements and arrangements, in order to achieve a balanced outcome.
